## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `learning-progress-exploration`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-09T10:35:29.359Z.

Planning pass 2026-07-09 (sixth follow-up): Algorithm (17) learning-progress-guided gap scheduling — an epistemic-foraging queue (serves pm-vvib candidate 18 curiosity drive). Purpose: rank what the workspace should LEARN next, so exploration (filling knowledge gaps) gets a principled, bounded share of agent attention alongside exploitation (pm next's ready work), using only signals that already exist. Mechanism, three stages. Stage 1 — gap-signal folding at write time (algorithm 6): maintain per-item and per-region (regions from algorithm 16 SR clusters, falling back to parent subtree via algorithm 9 chunking when the SR is too sparse) an uncertainty vector with four families: (a) completeness — count of absent high-value fields (AC, risk, confidence, resolution triple, close_reason), weighted by the item's retrieval frequency (algorithm 14 stage-1 sketch counters) so gaps in items agents actually USE outrank gaps in dead corners; (b) prediction residuals — per-region rolling error of the predictive layers (co-change algorithm 12: predicted-but-untouched and touched-but-unpredicted; SR algorithm 16: realized-trajectory divergence), folded as decaying counters (algorithm 1); (c) reliability blindness — retrieval-without-outcome ratio per precedent (served k times, zero confirmations/corrections from algorithm 14 stage 2), i.e. trust with no evidence; (d) isolation — hybrid-index neighborhood sparsity below a floor (no near neighbors = unreachable by association = invisible to spreading activation (2)). All sketch-backed (algorithm 8), O(1) amortized per mutation, replayable, no daemon (ADR pm-i7i4). Stage 2 — learning-progress estimator (the curiosity core): per region, track the DERIVATIVE of each error family over fold epochs; score curiosity as an explainable linear combination (algorithm 3) of gap magnitude × |error slope|, gated by the inverted-U: suppress mastered regions (error low and flat — nothing to learn) and unlearnable ones (error high and flat for M epochs — more sampling will not help; typically means missing instrumentation or genuinely chaotic territory, flagged once to validate instead of burning agent tokens). This is Oudeyer-style learning progress applied to a work corpus: attention flows to where the map is improvably wrong, and automatically withdraws as a region is either mastered or written off. Stage 3 — bounded exploration serving: the gap queue becomes one additional quota source in the retrieval funnel (algorithm 7) and an opt-in section of pm next — at most ONE gap-fill suggestion per envelope, rendered with its winning terms ("gap: release-tooling region — 12 retrieved-without-confirmation precedents, prediction error fell 40% last epoch, top item pm-XXXX missing risk+AC"), each suggestion a concrete enrichment action (add the missing field, confirm/correct the precedent, link the isolated item). Serving folds a curiosity-visit event so the same gap is not re-served while an agent works it (habituation, algorithm 13 stage 3 pattern; inhibition-of-return per agent derivable from its own stream). Explicitly NOT a new item generator by default: suggestions are actions on EXISTING items — item creation stays a human/agent decision, keeping the no-duplicates invariant intact. Distinct from (13) broadcast arbitration (pushes currently-salient EVENTS; this pulls toward stable KNOWLEDGE deficits), from (14) contradiction gating (corrects precedents PROVEN wrong; this targets precedents whose reliability is UNKNOWN), and from validate (static rule findings at a point in time; this is a dynamic, usage-weighted, progress-gated ranking over those findings plus model residuals). Spectrum behavior: small/young workspaces — error series too short, inverted-U gate keeps the quota empty, cost one fold per mutation; million-item decades-old workspaces — the corpus self-heals where it is used most, and the unlearnable-region flag gives maintainers a map of where instrumentation (not effort) is the missing ingredient. Completes the exploit/explore pair: algorithms 1–16 optimize serving what is known; 17 allocates attention to what is not.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
